ratings_why.fun: Over a 7 because the swap order turns one bank unit into the obstacle for every fish in a column, and the four answers to the Spawn cost (Kelt, Redd, Jack, Bradán) stack with the Bear and the Alder in ways the builds don't even list.
ratings_why.distinct: A passport plus swap-along-the-zigzag movement is new, but Spawn's trip home to hand with stats kept echoes the Birds' Fly South.

verdict_why: The engine is excellent; Old Kelt needs one line saying what happens to Stamps, or the lap build doesn't work as written.

points.text: Old Kelt doesn't say whether a Spawned fish's Stamps clear when it stays. If they don't, it never earns a 6th Stamp again and never re-Spawns, so the lap build stops; say they clear.

Weir-Jumper with Old Kelt and Llyn Llyw is a lovely hidden loop: three Fry deaths give six Stamps, a Spawn, three more Fry. Worth listing as a build and watching, since only board space and enemy attacks stop it.

The Bear with Old Kelt is a nice off-label use: force the Spawn, keep the body at the Mouth with +2/+2, and the Bear still takes half its stats. Say in the builds that the Bear is also Kelt's starter.
Fish-Pass Trout only moves fish. Giving it a small 'leapt past' hook of its own (it is swapped down when back-row fish rise) would let it join the Landlady trick instead of just feeding it.

Recruit-phase Leaps are only worth their Stamps and 'past' triggers, since you can rearrange freely. A card that cares where a fish ended the last fight would make the river's order matter between turns too.

standouts.why: Spawn on demand at any Stamp count turns the tribe's slow clock into a choice every turn, and it feeds Mother Redd, the Alder and Kelt at once.
With nearest-Head-first ordering, the sweep drags whatever sits above Kype past every fish below, so one Landlady or Ghillie fires four times.
Learn-then-forget makes a stored burst you time, and it doubles up with Little Jack and Old Kelt.

weakest.why: A plain Spawn buff to the team; it does the expected thing and nothing else.
Front-row-only is fiddly to track and mostly a weaker Landlady at Tier 4.
Pure enabler with no hook of its own.

flags.note: Stamps after a kept Spawn aren't stated, nor whether the fish still also comes home to hand.
With Llyn Llyw and Old Kelt, Fry deaths re-Spawn Weir-Jumper in a fight; Little Jack makes six Fry a Spawn.
With the Bear, a copy every turn means a triple and a Discover every couple of turns late on.
